title: LIKE SEEING THE FACE OF GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Esau asked, 'What's the meaning of all these flocks and herds I met?' 'To find favor in your eyes, my lord,' he said. But Esau said, 'I already have plenty, my brother. Keep what you have for yourself.' 'No, please!' said Jacob. 'If I have found favor in your eyes, accept this gift from me. For to see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favorably. Please accept the present that was brought to you, for God has been gracious to me and I have all I need.' And because Jacob insisted, Esau accepted it." - Gen 33:8-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob presses Esau to accept his gift, and in doing so he says something remarkable: "to see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favorably." Just the night before, at Peniel, Jacob had seen God "face to face" and been spared. Now, seeing the forgiving face of the brother he had wronged, he feels he is seeing the grace of God all over again.

There is a deep truth here. When someone we have hurt looks at us with forgiveness instead of anger, we catch a glimpse of what God's grace is like. Being reconciled to a brother can feel like meeting God Himself, because forgiveness is one of the clearest reflections of God's own heart.

Notice too Jacob's contentment: "God has been gracious to me and I have all I need." The grasping man who once wanted more, more, more, can now say he has enough. Esau says, "I have plenty"; Jacob says, "I have all I need." God's grace had made Jacob a contented man.

Two beautiful fruits of grace appear here: reconciliation that feels like heaven, and contentment that no longer grasps. May God grow both in us — the joy of forgiveness given and received, and a heart that rests satisfied in His grace (Phil 4:11-12).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I glimpsed God's grace in someone's forgiveness of me?
2. Can I say with Jacob, "God has been gracious to me and I have all I need"?
3. Where do I still grasp for more instead of resting in God's grace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that forgiveness reflects Your own gracious heart. Make me a person who both gives and receives grace, and teach me to rest content, saying, "I have all I need." Amen.
